verdict_reasoning: The bug is real and the reporter confirmed the fix on two platforms with three zlib versions, so nothing fails at level 1. Two fixable design points survive, and both concern the back-patch that message #3 asks for. maintenance-fit-1: v2-0002 bundles the pg_restore fix with a refactor of astreamer_gzip, which other tools use. standards-compat-1: zero-byte files and trailing bytes become errors. A committer who knows the frontend compression code has to decide the back-branch shape.

brief.title: Validate gzip streams in pg_restore with zlib inflate (bug #19754)
brief.problem: With zlib 1.3.2, gzread() and gzclose() can return wrong results, so pg_restore rejects valid gzip dump files whose sizes end on buffer boundaries and can accept truncated ones. This hits users restoring gzip-compressed dumps, including the Windows binaries of 14 to 18, which ship zlib 1.3.2.
brief.proposed_design: The patch moves the gzip decompression logic out of astreamer_gzip into a shared frontend helper in src/fe_utils/gzip.c that calls zlib's inflate() and lets callers handle errors. astreamer_gzip and pg_restore's compress_gzip.c both use it. pg_restore validates the stream through EOF, checks unread data at close, and supports concatenated gzip members.
user_visible_surface: pg_restore now rejects zero-byte gzip data files and trailing bytes after the last gzip member, per the tester's reading of the stricter parsing.
pg_restore reports a new truncation error, "compressed stream is incomplete".
New frontend C header src/include/fe_utils/gzip.h with a shared gzip decompression helper.
author_claims: The new TAP test 007_pg_dump_gzip.pl fails with zlib 1.3.2 without the fix and passes with it.
astreamer_gzip's push interface does not fit pg_restore's read interface, so the patch extracts a shared helper instead of reusing astreamer_gzip.
The reporter confirmed the fix on Debian 13 and Windows 11 with zlib 1.3.1, 1.3.2 and develop, including parallel restore, empty tables and large objects.
The reporter says pg_dump always writes at least an empty member, so the stricter parsing does not break dumps it produced.
The reporter asks for a back-patch to 14, noting that 14 and 15 lack compress_gzip.c and need their own fix.
brief.thread_state: The reporter tested v2 and asked for a back-patch. Daniel Gustafsson said he has the patch on his TODO list. No committer review or back-patch decision is visible.
unclear: The material does not say whether the stricter parsing rejects gzip dumps written by older pg_dump versions or third-party tools.
No back-patch plan exists for 14 and 15, which lack compress_gzip.c, or for 16 to 18.
The material does not say whether the new nls.mk entries add translatable strings, which matters for back branches.
The material does not say whether pg_basebackup, pg_verifybackup or pg_waldump change behaviour through the refactored astreamer_gzip.

prior_attempts.title: Revert "libpqwalreceiver: Convert to libpq-be-fe-helpers.h"
prior_attempts.quote: Since it was non-essential refactoring, let's revert it to make v16 work the same as earlier releases.
prior_attempts.reason:
This reverts commit 728f86fec65537eade8d9e751961782ddb527934.

The signal handling was a few bricks shy of a load in that commit,
which made the walreceiver non-responsive to SIGTERM while it was
waiting for the connection to be established. That prevented a standby
from being promoted.

Since it was non-essential refactoring, let's revert it to make v16
work the same as earlier releases. I reverted it in 'master' too, to
keep the branches in sync. The refactoring was a good idea as such,
but it needs a bit more work. Once we have developed a complete patch
with this issue fixed, let's re-apply that to 'master'.
prior_attempts.what_is_different: P18 was a pure refactor of libpqwalreceiver. This proposal is a bug fix that bundles a refactor of shared frontend code used by other tools.

objections.title: Back-patched bugfix also refactors astreamer_gzip, used by other tools
objections.failure_scenario: A packager ships a 16-18 minor release with this patch to fix pg_restore. The astreamer_gzip rework changes how pg_basebackup, pg_verifybackup or pg_waldump handle gzip input. A user finds this only when a backup check or WAL read starts to fail after a minor update.
objections.argument: Message #3 asks for a back-patch to 14, and v2-0002 moves the inflate logic out of astreamer_gzip into a new src/fe_utils/gzip.c. That moves code used by tools that have no reported bug. [P18] reverted a non-essential refactor from a released branch for this reason. 14 and 15 lack compress_gzip.c (message #3), so master's patch shape does not carry over, and the project would keep two or three versions of the fix.
objections.author_must_show: Can the series be split into a minimal back-patchable pg_restore fix and a separate master-only astreamer_gzip refactor, and what does the fix look like for 14 and 15?

critic.reasoning: The thread asks for a back-patch but gives no plan, and 0002 changes astreamer_gzip, which only recent branches have in fe_utils. [P18] concerns a different subsystem and gives only general support, but the objection holds without it.

objections.title: Stricter gzip parsing rejects files that pg_restore accepts today
objections.failure_scenario: A user keeps a directory-format dump that contains a zero-byte data file, or whose gzip files carry trailing padding from a copy or archive tool. After a minor upgrade that includes this fix, pg_restore stops with an error. The user finds out during a restore, possibly one run to recover lost data.
objections.argument: Message #3 confirms that zero-byte files and trailing bytes after the last member are now errors. The only argument offered is that current pg_dump always writes at least an empty member. That covers newly written dumps, but not dumps from older pg_dump releases or files that have been handled after pg_dump wrote them. gzip(1) accepts trailing zeros with a warning. A fix meant for back branches would likely be asked to keep the old acceptance or downgrade these cases to warnings.
objections.author_must_show: Has every pg_dump release that can write gzip directory or custom archives always written a non-empty gzip member, and why should trailing bytes be an error and not a warning?

critic.reasoning: Message #3 confirms that zero-byte files and trailing bytes become errors, and the thread only covers dumps written by current pg_dump. zlib's gzread() ignores extra trailing data today, so this changes behaviour in a minor release.

refuted.title: Bug fix bundles a refactor of astreamer_gzip shared by other tools
refuted.failure_scenario: A committer back-patches v2 to 16-18 to fix pg_restore. The moved inflate logic changes how astreamer_gzip handles concatenated members, trailing bytes or truncation. pg_basebackup or pg_verifybackup users on a minor release then see new errors on archives that worked before, and the cause is a refactor they never needed.
refuted.argument: In [P18], non-essential refactoring caused a regression in a released branch and was reverted from v16 and master. Here 0002 rewrites astreamer_gzip.c and touches nls.mk for pg_basebackup, pg_verifybackup and pg_waldump, while the bug sits only in compress_gzip.c. Message #1 says the helper exists because astreamer_gzip's push interface does not fit, which argues for a shared helper on master. It does not show that back branches need the refactor. Message #3 asks for a back-patch, and 14-15 already need a separate fix.
refuted.author_must_show: Can the back-branch fix touch only pg_restore's gzip read path and leave astreamer_gzip and the other tools unchanged?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of maintenance-fit-1, which makes the same point about the astreamer_gzip refactor in back branches and adds the request to split the series.

refuted.title: Back-patched bug fix also changes astreamer_gzip used by other tools
refuted.failure_scenario: A user on a back branch runs pg_basebackup or pg_verifybackup on a gzip backup after the minor release. The refactored astreamer_gzip handles an edge case differently, or prints a new message that has no translation. The user sees a difference in tools that were never affected by bug #19754.
refuted.argument: The bug is in pg_restore's use of gzread() and gzclose(), but v2 also rewrites astreamer_gzip and touches nls.mk for pg_basebackup, pg_verifybackup and pg_waldump. Message #3 asks for a back-patch to 14, and 14 and 15 need a separate fix anyway. [P18] records a back-branch revert because "it was non-essential refactoring, let's revert it to make v16 work the same as earlier releases." A committer would likely ask for a minimal pg_restore-only fix in back branches and keep the shared helper for master.
refuted.author_must_show: Can the back-branch fix be limited to compress_gzip.c, leaving astreamer_gzip and the messages of the other tools unchanged?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of maintenance-fit-1. Its point about new untranslated messages in back branches is valid and belongs with that objection.

refuted.title: Stricter gzip parsing may reject dump files that already exist
refuted.failure_scenario: After a minor release with the fix, a user restores a directory-format dump. It was written years ago by an older pg_dump, or its .dat files were recompressed with an external gzip tool. pg_restore now fails on a zero-byte data file or on trailing bytes, and the user finds out only when they need the restore.
refuted.argument: Dump archives are long-lived files, and pg_restore reads archives from many older pg_dump versions. The only evidence that nothing valid is rejected is message #3, which says current pg_dump always writes at least an empty member. Nothing covers older pg_dump releases or externally gzipped files. If the fix is back-patched as asked in message #3, the change lands in minor releases, where users do not expect a format check to tighten.
refuted.author_must_show: Which pg_dump versions, or which documented ways of producing directory-format files, can leave zero-byte gzip files or trailing bytes, and do they still restore?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-1. Its external recompression example is also weaker, because a gzip tool writes valid members without trailing bytes.

refuted.title: Back-patch also changes the gzip path for base backups
refuted.failure_scenario: A back-patched refactor of astreamer_gzip carries a subtle bug or changes the end-of-stream checks. pg_verifybackup then rejects a valid gzip base backup, or pg_basebackup fails to extract a server-compressed tar. The operator finds out during verification or recovery.
refuted.argument: The bug is in pg_restore, but v2-0002 moves the inflate logic out of astreamer_gzip, which pg_basebackup and pg_verifybackup use. The thread shows tests only for pg_restore, and message #3 asks for a back-patch to 14. [P18] records a back-branch revert of non-essential refactoring that broke a working path. A minimal pg_restore-only fix for the back branches would leave backup handling untouched.
refuted.author_must_show: Would the back-branch fix leave astreamer_gzip unchanged, and if not, what shows that gzip base backups still extract and verify unchanged?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of maintenance-fit-1. Its scenario of a subtle bug in the moved code is speculative, and the request for a minimal back-branch fix is the same.

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: The patch adds a shared frontend helper in src/include/fe_utils/gzip.h and changes astreamer_gzip to use it.

touch_points.label: pg_dump / restore round-trip
touch_points.reason: pg_restore now rejects zero-byte gzip data files and trailing bytes after the last gzip member.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: Message #3 asks for a back-patch to 14; 14 and 15 lack compress_gzip.c, and nls.mk changes touch four tools.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: Postgres takes over gzip stream handling from zlib's gzread(), and back branches may need two or three versions of the fix.

questions: Can the series be split into a minimal pg_restore-only fix for back branches and a master-only refactor of astreamer_gzip?
What does the fix look like for 14 and 15, which lack compress_gzip.c?
Has every pg_dump release that writes gzip archives always written at least one gzip member, so that no existing dump contains a zero-byte data file?
Why are trailing bytes after the last gzip member an error and not a warning, given that pg_restore accepts them today?
Does the refactored astreamer_gzip change behaviour or add translatable messages in pg_basebackup, pg_verifybackup or pg_waldump?

committability.owner_note: Daniel Gustafsson said the patch is on his TODO list, but no committer review is visible yet. The owner needs to know pg_dump's compression code and the astreamer code.
committability.liability: The owner signs for gzip reading in pg_restore on every branch that gets the fix, and for astreamer_gzip in pg_basebackup, pg_verifybackup and pg_waldump if the refactor is included. Dump files live for years, so a wrongly rejected archive can surface long after the release.
committability.author_follow_up: The author posted v2 one day after v1 to fix CI failures and asked the reporter to test.

priority.reason: Message #3 reports a production failure, and a truncated restore that exited 0, with zlib 1.3.2, which the Windows binaries of 14 to 18 ship. The 35 KiB fix touches pg_dump and shared fe_utils code, and back branches need their own versions.

provisional_note: Without the code, the review could not check whether the refactored astreamer_gzip behaves the same for the other tools, or whether memory use stays bounded on concatenated or malformed gzip members.

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_dump: optimize dumpFunc()
precedents_retrieved.summary: Replace pg_dump's per-function query in dumpFunc() with a single query that gathers data for all functions up front, keeping the PGresult in memory and using a sorted array of function OIDs to locate each function's row. The aim was to reduce dump time for databases with many functions (shown as about 0.25s to about 0.11s for 10k simple functions).
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane questioned whether the change helps databases with few functions and what it does to pg_dump's memory requirements when there are very many functions with large source text, and said the shown results did not justify the risk. The author agreed and withdrew the patch.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I'm not sure that the results you're showing justify taking any
risk here.

precedents_retrieved.title: Improve pg_dump dumping publication tables
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changes pg_dump's getPublicationTables() to fetch all publication-table memberships with a single query, instead of iterating over every table and issuing a separate query per table. The matching TableInfo for each row is then looked up in tblinfoindex, which should be faster when there are many tables.

precedents_retrieved.objection:
86ab7f4c721d commit made the table-level ON ERROR clause serve as the default
ON ERROR for columns lacking their own, so that a top-level ERROR ON ERROR
turned per-column evaluation errors into hard errors.

The SQL standard does mandate this cascade, but introducing it should be
a deliberate, separately-documented change, so restore the previous
behavior for now.  This also reverts the paired ruleutils.c logic that
deparsed a column's behavior against an ERROR default: that dropped an
explicit ERROR ON EMPTY from a dumped view, and otherwise emitted a
redundant NULL ON EMPTY.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent rejects the idea of replacing gzread()/gzclose() with inflate() in pg_restore. P3's zlib-variant risk applies only to test reproducibility, which is out of scope here.
The bug itself is real and shown by the reporter's tests. These objections concern how far the behaviour change reaches, mainly in back branches.
The patch adds no WAL, catalog, wire-protocol or server-side on-disk change. The objections above concern only existing dump and backup files read by frontend tools.

The patch changes how the client-side pg_restore checks gzip streams. It adds no privilege, role, server code or exposed data, and it now rejects truncated dumps that were silently accepted, so data integrity improves. Without the code, memory limits on concatenated or malformed members could not be checked.
The bug is real and confirmed by the reporter on two platforms, and a committer has said he will look at it. The only maintenance concern is the patch shape for back branches.

No existing feature covers this. The patch fixes wrong results from gzread() and gzclose() in zlib 1.3.2. Pinning or reverting zlib in the Windows packages, or running gunzip on directory-format files by hand, are workarounds for packagers and users, not a Postgres alternative. The patch also reuses the existing astreamer_gzip inflate() logic through a shared helper, so it does not add a second mechanism.

Demand is real. This is a bug fix for a field report: message #3 describes the failure seen in production with shipped Windows binaries of 14 to 18, and a restore that loaded 10073 of 20001 rows and exited 0. Users of gzip dumps with zlib 1.3.2 are a broad group, and no feature surface is added for a small group to pay for.
